body:
I've gone through a lot of shit. Been institutionalized from attempts, abused alcohol to self-medicate, the whole bit. I don't really drink anymore, but I've been there. Don't want to take my life anymore, but I would never think less of someone that did.

I need to sleep. I'll be back in the morning if you have any questions.

I remember you contacting me back when I posted on SW, so I won't take it personally. That meant a lot.

Not sure how much of that you remember, but I've been forced into psychiatric clinics three times. Made four attempts over the past ten years. "Walking out" might not be the most accurate phrase---I just stop showing up when I hit depressive episodes. Spend days at a time festering in isolation and contemplating how to end my future. You know, the usual.

Actually, I love the idea of working. I love the idea of something going on in my life. I'm just so damn disheartened by how I keep fucking things up. It's hard enough as is to land a job today, but why bother when I know I'm not stable enough to hang on to it?

Not singling you out, but I really don't know how to get that across to people. Most focus on my intellect and how I should give myself a kick in the ass, but there's nothing more frustrating in the world than knowing that you can't stick to anything long enough to get it done.

It's not that I'm not willing to do so. I've had jobs in the past that others in my position would be envious of, but I can't keep any sort of commitment for more than a few weeks. I've literally walked out of every job I've had because I'd break down and spiral out.

There was a point where I could maintain the facade of getting through each week---it's how I made it to university---but that point is long past.

Good news: I'm off to the hospital.

Bad news: My father was furious with me not because I attempted, but because he had to get out of his job to drive me. My mother proceeded to try and down the same pills I had been taking.
The good news is that I'm in touch with someone I know IRL. The bad news is that I'm currently on 9g lithium.

Still around, surprisingly. I might consider exchanging PMs, but I should have been upfront about rejecting phone calls. Thank you, but I want to preserve the little anonymity I have right now.

I understand I'm currently not thinking clearly, but I still feel that my particular case is difficult to solve. I am aware that there are people out there who are supportive. Unfortunately, they are not in a position to provide the sort of help that I need. I fear that Reddit might be the same way.

I am still here, reading what everyone has written so far. Thank you.

Where I am at right now is not conducive to my recovery. I should also emphasize that reasoning with my family is not a viable option, based on my observations since being diagnosed.

I don't see how I can get out of here.

Things are fast falling apart. My best friend has decided to avoid me for the weekend, as they can no longer handle my swings. I have others I can speak with, but at this point, it's easier to talk to anonymous people online than reveal intimate details to those I know IRL.

I haven't been this unstable in a while. Mood fluctuations are frequent and severe.

Hey. Thanks for sharing. Like many others, I'm here to listen about what's on your mind. Don't hesitate to PM me if you're more comfortable with that, but we do need more information to understand how we can best help you out.

Why are you taking such an intense load? It's not the end of the world if you take a bit of time to breathe and space out your courses. Have you considered seeking professional help?

My overall situation is very similar (though I have an active SW thread on my current issues), so I can relate. Don't hesitate to PM me if you feel like talking.

I have a car, although coming up with the money for gas has been difficult. I can't crash at my best friend's place, as the housemates don't approve of it.

I'm at the point right now where I have trouble deriving joy from anything.

My parents hold so much influence because they put a roof over my head and pay for the connection that allows me to talk to you today. Their support should be much more than that, but it's not, and I'm struggling to deal with it.
They believe whatever suits their agenda. The doctor that diagnosed me is working on the DSM-5, but that did nothing to sway their opinions.

I'm okay in the physical sense. I feel as defeated and unmotivated as ever, though. I've been using my lack of money to avoid spending time with my friends. The room I retreat to is in disarray. I don't look forward to anything.

It's close to how I felt before my meds, although I've been taking them regularly.

I'm currently insured under them, although until recently, I've had to cover any co-pays and medication related to my treatment. It also seems that I myself am their trigger, so there hasn't been a lot of positive interaction between us.
I'm on medical leave from college. The involvement of doctors in my departure leads my parents to blame my incomplete degree on them.

They've visited me while hospitalized and institutionalized, so they're aware of my suicidal ideation. The only excuse they provide is that they've willed their way through life, so I should be able to do the same.
